narrative.text:
NARRATIVE:

REMOVEABILITY:

Subject is removable per Section 237(a)(1)(B) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (Act), as amended, in that after admission as a nonimmigrant under Section 101(a)(15) of the Act, you have remained in the United States for a time longer than permitted, in violation of this Act or any other law of the United States.

Entry: Subject entered the United States at the Miami International Airport port of entry (MIA) on 12/23/2015.

TRAVEL DATA:

Subject traveled by bus to Houston, TX where he resided and worked as a part-time mechanic. On 4/12/2017 he boarded a bus with [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and arrived in Sault Sainte Marie on 4/14/2017. He then took another bus to Ann Harbor, MI where he was picked up by the smuggler and brought back to Sault Sainte Marie.

FACTS OF ARREST/ENCOUNTER:

At 0412 am, Sector Dispatch requested a Supervisory Border Patrol Agent contact Customs and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] Border Protection Supervisor [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] at the Sault Sainte Marie Port of Entry. SBPA called Supervisor [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and he informed SBPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] that the Canadian Customs Service Agency had apprehended a smuggling load of Nigerians and that there could possibly be more at the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] The driver of the vehicle claimed to Canadian Customs that he had rented this room. After advising Supervisory Border Patrol Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] of the situation, he and SBPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C] proceeded to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] and found that a [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , North York, Ontario, Canada had rented [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] the previous evening but according to the clerk, he was travelling alone. A check of the parking lot indicated no Canadian plated vehicles. SBPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] called Supervisor [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] who stated that [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was the driver of the smuggling load and was in Canadian custody. He advised me to call [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , the Canadian Customs Officer handling the case at [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] . Officer [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] advised that [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that he had travelled to Ann Arbor, Michigan yesterday morning and picked up 5 Nigerians, returning to Sault Sainte Marie, MI. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] stated that the two females and one male who were apprehended with [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] had obtained real documents and were found to be [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] imposters when they tried to enter Canada. Officer advised that [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] claimed two more Nigerians were in [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] at this time. Additional Border Patrol Agents were called in at 0630 am. SBPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] accompanied BPA's [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and they knocked on [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] . When a male opened the door, BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] announ were Border Patrol Agents and asked if they could come in and talk. The male, later identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , POB: Nigeria said yes, and additional agents entered into the room. A female was also found in the room, later identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , POB: Nigeria. Both subjects were advised that the U.S. Border Patrol had received information that additional Nigerian Nationals were in this room and were thought to be in the U.S. Illegally and were possibly going to attempt to try and illegally enter Canada. When question as to their citizenship, both claimed to be from Nigeria and both claimed to have entered the U.S. with passports as visitors.

BPA [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] obtained both Subjects passports and ran checks through Sector Dispatch. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , POB: Nigeria entered as a B1/B2 arriving on 12-23-2015 at MIA, admitted to 06-22-2016, with a departure date of 01-10-2016. [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] reveals [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] to be an Overstay. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , POB: Nigeria entered as a B-1/B2 arriving on 06- 01-2016 with a departure date of 06-09-2016. [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] reveals [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] to be an Overstay. Subjects were arrested and transported to [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station for processing.

IMMIGRATION HISTORY:

Subject arrived at Miami on 12/23/2015 and was admitted as a B2 Visitor until 06/22/2016.

CRIMINAL HISTORY:

No criminal history found.

HEALTH:

Subject appears to be in good health.

EQUITIES:

Subject has $6,638.00 (USD) in possession. All money was transferred with subject to [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] County Jail.

DISPOSITION:

Subject is being held in Service custody pending a hearing at a time and place to be determined. Subject is currently lodged in the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] County Jail. Subject was served a Warrant of Arrest/Notice to Appear, Notice of Custody, and was provided a list of free legal services.
